# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)

**Governing policy:** Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index (Knee Arthroplasty v8, Knee Arthroscopy v10, Hip Arthroplasty v5, Hip Arthroscopy v6, Shoulder Arthroplasty v4, Shoulder Arthroscopy v5, Open Shoulder v4, Cervical Spinal Fusion v5, Lumbar Spinal Fusion v3, Spinal Decompression v4.1, Ankle Arthroplasty v4, Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3)
URL: https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-17, Reference number POC-A389519C6D-33639
**Member:** Quinn Delgado
**Member ID:** W570305899
**Plan:** Avera Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), South Dakota

To Whom It May Concern:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction, CPT 28296), which I received notice of on 2026-08-17. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking Avera Health Plans to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial states that this procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. The notice identifies the applicable review criteria as coming from the Avera Health Plan Commercial Guidelines, and specifically references a guideline set that includes "Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3." The index of guidelines confirms this:

> "All Collections Review Criteria Avera Health Plan Avera Health Plan:"

> "Commercial/Medicaid & Medicare Advantage Guidelines Review Criteria:"

However, the denial notice I received did not quote the specific clinical thresholds or requirements from the Great Toe Surgical Treatments guideline that my case was measured against. I am not able to show point-by-point how my records meet criteria I have not been given in writing. What I can state clearly is what my medical records document, so that the plan can compare that documentation directly to its own guideline:

- **Duration and impact:** I have had 18 months of progressive pain in my foot that has not improved with rest.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:** I completed 12 weeks of physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25), including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** I used NSAIDs for 8 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that gave only about 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken 2026-06-07 showed a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- **Functional limitation:** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is documented risk of ulceration over the bony prominence.
- **Exam findings:** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- **No disqualifying factors:** There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I am a non-smoker.

This is a case where I have completed a substantial course of non-surgical treatment without lasting relief, and where imaging and exam findings are documented in my chart. I am asking the plan to explain, specifically, which part of the Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3 guideline it found unmet, and to review this record against that guideline in full.

## Request for the exact criteria applied

Because the denial notice did not quote the specific clinical criteria used to evaluate my request, I am formally asking Avera Health Plans to provide me, in writing, the exact clinical criteria applied to this denial, including the name and edition of the review guideline (for example, the specific version of the Great Toe Surgical Treatments guideline referenced above). I understand I am entitled to this information, and I would like to review it alongside my medical records.

## Deadline and where to send this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-13** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter. If that address is not available to me, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Avera Health Plans to reconsider this denial, to review the clinical documentation summarized above against the Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3 guideline (or whichever guideline was actually applied), and to provide me with a written copy of the specific criteria used in this determination. I am also asking Dr. Marchetti's office to be contacted directly if any additional clinical documentation is needed to complete this review.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Quinn Delgado]
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Member ID: W570305899

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
